tool.name: TaxonMapping

param.name: db_file
param.dialogReference:
Working GeoPackage (.gpkg) database file. Will be created if it doesn't exist.

The resulting mapping can be viewed in the mappings table (read-only). The tracking_taxa table contains the entire tracking list, and the inat_taxa table contains all taxa for which a corresponding iNaturalist taxon was found. You may manually edit these two tables in the ArcGIS Pro interface, such as removing taxa that don't actually match from inat_taxa. The read-only not_in_inat table shows all of the tracking list entries with no matching iNaturalist taxon.

param.name: inat_user
param.dialogReference: The iNaturalist username to query taxa with. The credentials for this account must be registered in the system credential manager.

param.name: tracking_csv
param.dialogReference: A Biotics tracking list generated by the Biotics Query Builder using the query given in docs\biotics_query.sql. The tool will search for each taxa in iNaturalist and create a mapping if a match is found.

param.name: overrides_csv
param.dialogReference:
A csv file containing manual name overrides to use when searching instead of a taxon's Biotics name. It should contain the following columns:

  • est_id (integer). Element subnational tracking ID.

  • inat_name (string). Scientific name to use instead of the Biotics one.

  • taxon_id (integer). The taxon's iNaturalist ID, if known.

Each row must include either inat_name or taxon_id. If both are present, the override name will be ignored.

Most of the time you'll only have the override names, in which case the taxon_id column may be all blank. But if iNaturalist's search function is being particularly stubborn, you can include the exact ID of the iNaturalist taxon that matches the Biotics one. The tool will ignore the scientific names entirely and search directly by taxon ID. It still searches for these taxa to verify that the IDs actually exists.

tool.summary: Creates a mapping between tracking list taxa and iNaturalist taxa. Requests taxon names and IDs from the iNaturalist API. Inserts trackinglist and iNaturalist mapping into a GeoPackage database.
tool.usage:
If starting from scratch, it's recommended to run the tool in batches rather than on the whole tracking list at once. The tool will take about 1 second per taxon.

The tracking list file should be generated in the Biotics Query Builder using the query given in docs/biotics_query.sql.
